title: Tensor algebra word basis from a vector-space basis
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $V$ a $k$-vector space, and $(b_i)_{i\in I}$ a basis, where $I$ is any set. Let $T_k(V)$ be the tensor algebra with canonical linear map $\iota:V\to T_k(V)$: it is the unital associative $k$-algebra universal for linear maps from $V$, meaning that every linear map from $V$ to a unital associative $k$-algebra $A$ extends uniquely to a $k$-algebra homomorphism $T_k(V)\to A$. Let $k\langle I\rangle$ be the free associative $k$-algebra: its underlying vector space has basis the finite words in $I$, including the empty word, and multiplication of basis words is concatenation. Write $X_i$ for the one-letter word $i$. There is a canonical $k$-algebra isomorphism $T_k(V)\simeq k\langle I\rangle$ sending $\iota(b_i)$ to $X_i$. The elements $\iota(b_{i_1})\cdots\iota(b_{i_n})$, indexed by all finite words $(i_1,\ldots,i_n)$ in $I$, form a $k$-basis of $T_k(V)$; the empty word gives $1$.
